clue.text: Open discussion at 3pm perhaps

definitions.meaning: to open a debate is to start it off, a verb sense
the traditional starting time of a Saturday football match in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone schedules a meeting to begin mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football the classic Saturday start time is 3pm, so the starting moment of a match fits the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean the start: of a discussion as a verb, of a football match as a noun.

clue.text: Cover for a young goat

parts.note: reads as a coat for a kid, but means leather made from a kid's hide

explanation.definitionFit: Fine leather from a kid's hide, used for gloves.

clue.text: Rare object of despicable person I love!

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A lover's exclamation about a rotten partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity, an unusual collectable item.

clue.text: Decree that one should enter the artillery

indicators.note: the letter for one goes into the middle of the artillery word

parts.note: ordnance means artillery and military supplies
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An order that a soldier join the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official order or local law.

clue.text: Note I've a franc outside

indicators.note: the franc letters sit on either side of I've

parts.note: FR is an abbreviation for franc
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone notes they have a French coin on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pound banknote in British slang.

clue.text: What the drudge noticed in the tool-shed?

definitions.text: What the drudge noticed in the tool-shed?

parts.note: a hack is a drudge, someone doing dull routine work
saw means noticed

explanation.surface: A tired labourer glances round the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool for metal, exactly the kind of thing kept in a shed.

clue.text: No end of gin hesitantly carried by Dutchman

indicators.note: removes the final letter of the gin word, leaving it without its end

parts.note: Hollands is a Dutch gin
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A Dutchman carrying gin falters over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' drops the last S from HOLLANDS, a Dutch gin; 'carried by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Holland is a Netherlander.

clue.text: Heavenly body to arrive on time

parts.note: come means arrive

explanation.surface: Something in the sky turns up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body orbiting the sun with a tail.

clue.text: Coastline breaks up in parts

indicators.note: breaking up a word means splitting and rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Erosion shatters the shore into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of sections comes in separate pieces.

clue.text: We called and left during the dispute

indicators.note: the called and left letters come in the middle of we

parts.note: rang means called on the phone

explanation.surface: Two people phoned and walked out mid-argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a long, noisy argument.

clue.text: Courageous, having risked vile concoction

parts.note: dared means risked

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up, so the letters of vile are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone braves a nasty brew.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, bold person, used as an adjective for fearless.

clue.text: Coffee and, after a short time, tea

indicators.note: places the tea piece after the short-time piece

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a short time
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: An order for coffee, then tea a moment later.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of fine coffee, named for a Yemeni port.

clue.text: Now in the outskirts of Kingston, it is understood

indicators.note: the word now sits inside the other letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters of Kingston are used

explanation.surface: A remark that everyone knows things are happening on the edge of Kingston now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' gives K and N, the first and last letters of Kingston.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood is recognised or familiar.

clue.text: The genuine article could be large and thin

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something authentic might be both large and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins; the anagram is of LARGE plus THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the authentic item rather than an imitation.

clue.text: No collier said by Edward to have been proposed

indicators.note: said signals that the coal-worker word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward claims no coal-miner was ever put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put forward as a candidate is being proposed.

clue.text: Silent parent has an opportunity

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: A mother gets her opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: MUMCHANCE is an old word for silent and tongue-tied.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for mute or tongue-tied.

clue.text: His parents out east arranged move

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out says the east letter is dropped from the words

explanation.surface: His parents arranged a move out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the E of HISPARENTS; 'arranged' rearranges the remaining HISPARNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To move cargo from one ship to another vessel.

clue.text: Had chosen sensitive part. Understand

indicators.note: only a part of the words chosen sensitive is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone picked a delicate spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense is to grasp or perceive.

clue.text: Trivial half pint

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom calls minor matters weak ale; literally, a modest glass of ale is small.

clue.text: Battle memos flying about

indicators.note: papers flying about are scattered, so the letters of memos are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wartime messages scattered in a field office.
explanation.definitionFit: A major First World War battle in northern France.

clue.text: Blow for man with two companies at loggerheads

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a man

indicators.note: facing each other in opposition, so one of the company abbreviations is turned to face the other

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, used twice
the second CO for company

explanation.surface: A man whose two firms are feuding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at loggerheads' turns one CO into OC, so the two face each other: OC CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dusty wind from North Africa; blow means a gust of wind.

clue.text: Posted overseas?

parts.note: reads like a soldier stationed abroad, but means sent letters by aeroplane

explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent abroad usually goes by aircraft.

clue.text: Senior female member was swindled accepting Japanese currency

indicators.note: the swindled word takes in the currency, holding it inside

parts.note: done means cheated, as in I was done
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A senior woman was cheated over yen payments.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior woman of a group, the female form of doyen.

clue.text: Prepared to play

parts.note: reads as ready to begin, but means having practised a play or piece beforehand

explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise lines in advance of a performance.

clue.text: Be of assistance when a small number suffer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a small number
ail means suffer or be ill

explanation.surface: Help is needed when a few people fall ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or be of use.

clue.text: Same again, mostly affluent Greek architecture

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same again

indicators.note: most of the word for affluent, losing its last letter

parts.note: rich means affluent

explanation.surface: Ordering another round, mostly in wealthy Greek style.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest and plainest of the classical Greek orders of columns.

clue.text: Tending to lose water — or secret information

definitions.text: Tending to lose water — or secret information

parts.words: Tending to lose water — or secret information
parts.note: a pipe or roof that drips, or an organisation whose secrets slip out to the press

explanation.definitionFit: Something with holes drips; a sieve-like office lets out confidential facts.

clue.text: Entertain Urania?

definitions.meaning: to make people laugh or occupy them pleasantly
Urania was one of the nine Muses, of astronomy, so she is one

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to divert; read as two words, one of the goddesses inspiring the arts.

clue.text: Dance with Georgia

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone takes a partner called Georgia onto the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American line dance with a kick on every fourth beat.

clue.text: Rugby player in pantomime

definitions.meaning: A London rugby union club, so a player is one of them
a character in the traditional pantomime, the masked clown in diamond costume

explanation.surface: A rugby star turns up in the Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show; the masked clown in chequered tights is a stock character of the old harlequinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the London club member and the stock comic servant of the harlequinade share the name.

clue.text: Cover and extend beyond more than one circuit

parts.note: over means more than
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A runner does extra distance past the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that partly lie across each other each extend past the other's edge.

clue.text: One is late for this train

definitions.text: One is late for this train

parts.words: One is late for this train
parts.note: sounds like a delayed passenger, but the late one is the deceased and the train a funeral procession

explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession follows the dead person, the late one.
